Triage: first-touch graded — promoted `finding` → `pm:queue`, `bug`. (Triage seat, session `session_0185aJyu6TRnHbcVgSfGPSho`.)

Rationale: worse than the sibling it was swept from in the one dimension that matters for authoring — a swallowed load failure renders as a completed empty picker with **no trace at all**, silently steering operators toward "no fields/objects/views exist" conclusions (and toward creating duplicates). Three loaders, one file, one class, and the fix shape is already landed one screen away (#5110's discriminated union). Dispatch as one change, not three; the pickers need an error state that does not exist today, so this adds copy as well as an arm. Sibling: #5169 (same sweep, same file family) — a single claim covering both is acceptable if the file surfaces are declared together.

Container & model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus`.
Clause-②: no — adds a UI state to an internal admin surface. No published contract moves, no accept set changes.
Serial constraints cleared: declared under this seat's maintainer-granted **app-shell sub-directory-level exemption**, so the four substitute disciplines bind you: ① this region declaration is file-level; ② **merge `main` before opening the PR**; ③ merge again once any sibling app-shell card lands; ④ conflicts go to the merge queue, ⛔ never hand-ordered. `ResourceEditPage.tsx` has no open PR against it, and #5169's file (`AuditPanel.tsx`) is a different file in the same directory.

## The defect, and why it is worse than the card it came from

Three effects in `ResourceEditPage.tsx` feed the editor's option pickers — object names; the selected object's fields + actions; the selected object's views. All three `catch` by writing **the same value a successful empty response writes**, then flip loading to false. The picker renders as a completed, empty list.

They are the exact shape #5110 was filed for, with one difference that cuts the wrong way: **#5110 at least left a `console.error`. These leave nothing at all** — no error state, no banner, no log.

`client.list()` throws for every non-ok status except 404, so these swallow refusals, dropped connections, expired sessions and unparseable bodies alike, and render all of them as "there is nothing here".

**The user-visible reading is the point of the card**: an operator authoring a view, a permission row or an action reads the empty picker as the metadata graph's answer — *this object has no fields* — and an author who concludes that tends to go and create one. The honest answer is that the question was never answered.

## Zone 1 — the fix shape is already landed one screen away

⛔ Do not invent a pattern. #5110 landed the target shape **in this same file**: a discriminated union per loader (`idle | loading | loaded | error`) so a fault cannot be spelled as a measurement, plus a picker that says it could not load rather than showing none. Mirror it. Three loaders, one file, one class — **one change, not three**.

Read #5110's landed diff first; matching an established shape beats inventing a second one, and this seat has already ruled that way once this round.

## The one thing that differs from #5110, stated so you don't over-copy

**These pickers have no empty-state copy of their own today.** #5110 was partly about keeping an existing sentence honest; here there is no sentence — what is missing is a state that **does not exist at all**. So this is additive UI, not a rewrite of existing copy. Do not manufacture an "empty" sentence you were not asked for; add the *failure* state and let the genuinely-empty case stay as it is.

## Zone 2 — PM mechanism assumption (verify)

I expect all three loaders can share one small state helper rather than three hand-rolled unions. If the three differ enough that sharing distorts them, say so and write three — but say which you chose. Three copy-pasted unions in one file is how the next drift starts.

## Tests

Pin, per loader: a **failed** load renders the failure state and **not** an empty list; a genuinely **empty successful** load still renders the empty list; and the loading flag clears in both. That triple is what separates "no options" from "could not ask". A test that only asserts the happy path proves nothing here — the bug lives entirely in the catch.

## Gates

Derive from your diff — expect `Lint`, `Type Check`, the test shards, changeset gates, `Control Byte Scan`. Changeset required (`@object-ui/app-shell`, patch). Re-derive against what you actually changed.

## Deliver

Draft PR against `main`, first line `Fixes #5170`. Push the branch early. Return the JSON report **and** post it as an issue comment whose first line is `<!-- os-dev-report -->`. Read the full issue body and all comments on GitHub yourself; check the body for sanitizer truncation before relying on it.
